title: Associativity of the canonical translated-unit comparison
statement: Let X be a scheme with its derived category, recorded tensor [def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure], canonical tensor shifts [def-sc-scheme-canonical-tensor-shift], and c_X [def-sc-scheme-canonical-shift-unit-iso]. For all K,M in D(O_X), c_X(K tensor M) is the inverse associator from O_X[1] tensor (K tensor M) to (O_X[1] tensor K) tensor M, followed by c_X(K) tensor id_M and the canonical first-variable shift s_(tensorRight M)(1)_K. This identity concerns one scheme and has no pullback or triangulated-functor assertion.

source.place: Canonical K-flat total tensor translation; translated-unit calculation of the parent plan

proof.text: Expand schemeCanonicalShiftUnitIso as the first-variable shift comparison at the tensor unit followed by the shifted left unitor. The private proved helper tensorShiftUnitCalculation performs the remaining categorical calculation in an arbitrary monoidal category with shifted right-tensor functors.

Apply the canonical first-variable associator square with A the tensor unit and n=1. This identifies the shift comparison followed by the shifted inverse associator with the inverse associator followed by the two successive shift comparisons.

Use Mathlib leftUnitor_tensor_hom to expand the left unitor of K tensor M. Map that composite under the shift functor and apply the preceding square. Naturality of (tensorRight M).commShiftIso at (leftUnitor K).hom moves the shifted unitor across the second comparison. Functoriality of right whiskering then recombines the first comparison with the shifted left unitor, giving exactly the stated equality. All these steps are proved in the private generic helper.
